source.title: Derry Journal, 6 June 1930, p. 7 ("Tyrone local government elections"); Ulster Herald, 7 June 1930, p. 5 ("Tyrone elections: results of contests"); Belfast News-Letter, 23 May 1930, p. 3
source.publisher: Derry Journal (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: votes and majority as printed: 'Castlecaulfield Division - Colonel R. J. Howard (official Unionist), 712; W. J. M'Mullan (Indpt. U.), 603. Official Unionist majority, 109' (Derry Journal, 6 June 1930); the Ulster Herald of 7 June prints the same result and gives the total poll as 1,325 with ten rejected papers. Citation confirmed 6 Nov 2026: all surnames and most figures found in the page text.

note: Poll date confirmed: 'Polling took place yesterday in the contested County Council divisions of Fermanagh and Tyrone, the results of which will be declared to-day' (Belfast News-Letter, 5 June 1930, p. 9) - Wednesday 4 June 1930. Two Tyrone divisions were contested. Castlecaulfield: Colonel R. J. Howard (official Unionist) 712, W. J. M'Mullan (Independent Unionist) 603, majority 109, total poll 1,325, 10 rejected (Ulster Herald, 7 June 1930, p. 5; Derry Journal, 6 June 1930, p. 7). Coalisland: Patrick Hagan (Nat.) 799, Patrick M'Grath (Nat.) 296, majority 503, total poll 1,102, 7 spoiled (Derry Journal, 6 June 1930, p. 7; Ulster Herald, 7 June 1930, p. 5). The same Ulster Herald report, headed 'The new County Council', names the members returned for the other divisions: 'The candidates who have been returned unopposed are as follows' - Ballygawley, Carrickmore, Castlederg, Clogher, Coagh, Cookstown, Douglas, Dromore, Dunbreen, Donemana, Moy, Newtownstewart, Omagh Rural, Pomeroy and Trillick - and the preceding paragraph names the changes at Aughnacloy, Benburb, Fintona, Stewartstown, Strabane, Plumbridge and Killeter. Dungannon is not named at all in the 1930 report, either among the changes or in the printed unopposed list; the division and name are supplied from the Strabane Chronicle's complete 1939 list (D. G. Kennedy, J.P., U.), the same source used for the 1933 round. Two further uncontested changes are printed without the name of the division: Mr. Michael Lynch succeeding Mr. A. E. Donnelly, M.P., and Mr. James O'Neill succeeding Mr. Michael M'Anallen, J.P. The 1927 return, read later, places Donnelly at Omagh Urban and M'Anallen at Donaghmore, and the file assigns them there. That same 1927 return shows Thomas Stewart at Strabane, so Gallagher's succession at Strabane is measured against Stewart, not Donnelly: Stewart moved to Plumbridge when Lynch moved to Omagh Urban. The Irish News of 10 June 1930, p. 6 says the elected council was 10 Nationalists and 14 Unionists (24), with Mr. Joseph Mills an independent Unionist. Uncontested divisions here reflect a deliberate abstention, not missing coverage: in the Omagh Rural District, Nationalists refused to nominate against Unionist-held seats in every year except 1949, when only 4 of 21 such seats were contested (Kingsley 2021, 'The Omagh Rural District Electoral Divisions Scheme 1923', citing PRONI LA/62/2/FA/38 and Ulster Herald 10 Feb 1923). See notes/tyrone-county-council_absent_contests.txt Howard was chairman of the County Council; M'Mullan stood as an Independent. The Ulster Herald's count report says eight rejected papers were marked '2' for M'Mullan and two voters polled for both candidates.
